rawLog.content: Kan waits for Itachi in the rain.

Cold October rain needles through the pine canopy, plastering your dark hair to your forehead and soaking the heavy wool of your cloak until it drags at your shoulders like lead. Beneath your boots, a thick mat of wet needles and rotting leaves gives way to mud. Two miles back, beyond the black ridge and the mist-choked valley, Konoha sits under a suffocating lockdown—specifically the walled compound at its edge, where the rainwater running into the gutters has not yet washed clean. Out here, there is only the relentless hiss of the downpour and the faint, metallic tang of blood that seems to have followed you on the wind.

A crow's wing cuts the dark without a sound. There is no snap of a twig, no splash in the mire; the shadows beneath an ancient cedar simply thicken and take shape. Itachi steps out from behind the trunk, his ANBU armor discarded for a high-collared black cloak that swallows his frame. The rain slicks the deep, exhausted troughs beneath his eyes, and in the pitch gloom beneath the branches, the three tomoe of his Sharingan burn like dying embers. A diagonal slash sits freshly across the leaf symbol of his forehead protector.

He stops five paces away, hands hidden inside the folds of his cloak, though the faint scent of iron and ozone still clings to him despite the storm. For a long beat, he only looks at you, his face as pale and still as carved bone while water drips from his chin.

"You shouldn't have waited this close to the perimeter, Kan," Itachi says, his voice quiet, flat, and worn raw beneath the drumming rain. "Root hounds will have the scent trails before dawn. If you're still standing here when the sun comes up, Danzo won't bother asking questions."
"did you do it?" *i ask, referring to his plan to kill the Uchiha clan."

Itachi does not flinch, nor does he look away. For several seconds, the only answer is the steady drumming of rain against the pine needles and the trickle of water running down the deep lines beside his mouth. Slowly, he draws his right hand from beneath the folds of his black cloak. The pale skin of his fingers is washed clean by the storm, except for the crescent beds of his fingernails, where a dark, rust-colored stain remains stubbornly wedged. 

"It is done," Itachi says softly, each word dropping like a stone into dark water. His red eyes dim for a fraction of a second as his eyelids lower, though the Sharingan does not fade. "All of them. Except for Sasuke." The name of your former teammate, Izumi, hangs unspoken in the freezing air between you, heavy and suffocating, swallowed by that simple, absolute *all of them*. 

Before the silence can settle, a sharp, metallic whistle cuts through the hiss of the downpour—a signal flare bursting high above the tree line a half-mile toward the village wall, painting the underside of the storm clouds a brief, sickly green. Seconds later, the distant, rhythmic baying of tracker hounds echoes across the ravine, followed by the faint, rapid thrum of three—no, four—sets of footsteps moving across the high branches to the east. A perimeter sweep from the Inuzuka and ANBU sentry squads, closing the net faster than expected.

Itachi glances once toward the green glow fading in the mist, then turns his gaze back to you, stepping close enough that you can feel the feverish heat radiating off his soaked clothes. "That's a four-man hunter cell," he murmurs, his voice dropping to an urgent, quiet rasp. "If you go back now, you tell the Third you were tracking me and lost my trail in the wash. You keep your mask, your life, and whatever is left of your place in the sun. Or you come with me into the dark—into an organization called Akatsuki—and help me watch the monsters who helped light this fire from the inside. Decide now, Kan. They'll have this ridge in sixty seconds."
*I think for a second, in that one second, options, choices, different life paths, all flash in front of my eyes* "did you kill your lover?"

For the span of a single heartbeat, the absolute stillness that makes Itachi a phantom in the ANBU cracks. The muscles along his jaw tighten, and the three black tomoe spinning lazily in his crimson eyes blur into a sharp, pinwheel pattern—a jagged, bleeding shape you have never seen before—before snapping back into three distinct dots. A single, thin thread of dark blood wells at the inner corner of his right eye, immediately diluted into pink and washed down his pale cheek by the driving rain.

"She died in peace," Itachi whispers, his voice so low the drumming rain nearly swallows it whole. His gaze drops for a fraction of a second to the mud between your boots before rising back to your face, colder and more hollow than before. "She lived an entire lifetime before her heart stopped. I made sure she didn't feel the blade, Kan. She was the first."

East of the ridge, a heavy branch snaps under the weight of a leaping hound. A sharp, familiar bark cuts through the downpour—higher-pitched and faster than the deep baying of the heavy tracker dogs. With your shared history on Team 3, you know that cadence instantly: it is one of the Haimaru brothers. Hana is on the ridge, running point for the ANBU cell closing in on your position, less than three hundred yards away through the black trees.

Itachi hears it too. His head tilts slightly toward the sound, his body already coiling to vanish into the canopy, one hand reaching out to grip the wet fabric of your cloak at the shoulder. "Hana is with them," he says quietly, the urgency sharpening his words like whetted steel. "If she sees you standing beside me, she will have to mark you as a traitor or die trying to take us in. Thirty seconds, Kan. Konoha, or the dark with me?"
"looks like I don't have a choice. once they get here and realize our smells met here, they will know that we met here. they won't trust me."

A faint, joyless shadow of a smile touches the corner of Itachi’s mouth, vanishing almost before it forms. "Ever the pragmatist," he murmurs, though there is a quiet, aching weight in his tone that betrays how much he wished you still had a clean road back. His fingers tighten on the sodden wool of your shoulder, and with his free hand, he reaches into his cloak and draws a kunai. Before he moves, he turns the blade toward you, holding it out by the wrapped handle, its steel glinting dull gray in the dark. "Scratch your headband, or leave the mask in the mud. If Danzo’s people think you were taken against your will, they’ll hunt you differently than if they know you walked away."

Through the sheets of rain to the east, the brush explodes outward as three sleek, gray-furred blurs bound over a fallen rotting log—the Haimaru triplets, noses low to the churned earth despite the downpour. Right behind them, a familiar figure in an ANBU vest and red fang-markings drops from a low cedar bough, landing in a splash of muddy water less than eighty yards out. Even through the curtain of storm and shadow, you catch the sharp snap of Hana’s head as the wind shifts, bringing the mingled scent of rainwater, wet wool, and Uchiha blood straight into her lungs.

"Wait—stop!" Hana’s voice rings out through the trees, sharp and tight with sudden recognition, cutting off the deeper bark of the lead ANBU captain drop-stepping behind her. "That secondary scent—it isn't Root. Hold your fire, someone from our side is up ahead!"

Itachi’s chakra flares cold and sharp against your arm, priming for a Body Flicker that will carry you both beyond the valley ridge before the hounds can close the last fifty yards. His red eyes lock onto yours, waiting for your final move before he pulls you into the slipstream—whether to sever your tie to the Leaf right here in front of her, or vanish without a word.
*I look at the mask one last time, And drop it. I take my headband out of my pocket and scratch it* "no turning back, huh?"

The porcelain ANBU mask hits the mud with a dull, wet *thwack*, its painted red markings staring blankly up into the driving rain as dirty water immediately begins to pool in the eye slits. When you draw the kunai across the steel plate of your forehead protector, the screech of metal tearing metal is small and sharp—a thin, violent rasp that nonetheless cuts straight through the drumming downpour. 

Fifty yards away, the Haimaru triplets skid to a halt in the churned pine needles, their hackles rising as they let out a chorus of low, confused whines. Hana freezes on a thick cedar root just behind them, her dark eyes widening as they adjust to the gloom beneath the canopy. She sees the pale oval of your discarded mask in the mud first, then follows the line of your arm up to the freshly gouged steel in your hand, and finally to the crimson glow of Itachi’s Sharingan beside you. For a heartbeat, the fierce tracker vanishes, replaced by the girl from Team 3—her lips parting in a silent breath, her rain-slicked face slack with raw disbelief.

"Kan?" she breathes, the name barely carrying over the wind before the heavy silhouette of her squad captain—a broad-shouldered ANBU in a horned boar mask—drops from the branches beside her, two fingers already raised to his lips to form a hand seal.

"Don't hesitate, Inuzuka! That's the target and an accomplice!" the boar-masked captain barks, his voice muffled by porcelain as lightning crackles across the wet bark at his feet. "Box them in—*Fire Style!*"

"No turning back," Itachi echoes softly, his fingers locking like iron around your shoulder just as the captain's chest swells with superheated breath. The world blurs into a tunnel of screaming wind and black pine needles as Itachi's Body Flicker yanks you both backward into the canopy, though a stray tongue of the captain's fire clips the branch beneath your boots, sending a shower of hissing embers and scalding steam straight into your face as the dark forest swallows Konoha behind you.
*the life i lived in the hidden leaf flashes before my eyes, my childhood, gone just like that, now I need to live a different life*

The wind tears at your soaked cloak as you and Itachi vault from bough to slick bough, putting miles of black pine and jagged ravines between yourselves and the roaring orange glow of the ANBU captain's fire. With every kick against the wet bark, pieces of the last thirteen years peel away and fall behind you into the dark: the sun-baked dirt of Training Ground Three, Suzume-sensei's sharp voice correcting your posture, Izumi's quiet smile after a long mission, and the fierce, bewildered hurt in Hana's eyes just moments ago. The baying of the Haimaru triplets fades from a sharp chorus into a hollow, distant echo, until even that is swallowed by the roaring white noise of the storm and the river gorge rushing below.

Three miles out, where the ancient cedars thin into a jagged limestone ridge overlooking the border valley, Itachi suddenly kills his momentum. He drops onto a slick shelf of rock beneath an overhanging cliff, his hand catching your chest to haul you back into the deep shadow just as the air ten paces ahead of you *twists*. It isn't a sound or a flash of chakra; the rain simply stops falling in a tight, spiraling funnel, the water droplets bending inward as if sucked into a drain hung in mid-air. 

From the center of that warping vortex, a tall figure materializes on the boulder across the ledge. He wears a long black cloak patterned with red clouds that hang heavy with rain, and a pale orange mask carved with ridges that swirl inward toward a single, bottomless black eye-hole. In the shadowed socket behind that hole, a solitary, blood-red Sharingan gleams—unrelated to Itachi's, ancient and cold, watching the two of you with detached amusement.

"And here I thought our deal was for one stray crow, Itachi," the masked man says, his voice a deep, resonant baritone that vibrates against the wet stone despite the howling wind. His single crimson eye shifts slowly from Itachi’s pale face to rest squarely on you, weighing the freshly scratched steel of your headband and the ANBU tanto strapped to your back. "You left the compound in quite a mess, and now you bring a little half-breed shadow clinging to your coattails. Tell me, boy... do you even know what kind of ghosts you're walking away with tonight, or should I save Konoha the trouble and cull the last loose end right here?"
"so you didn't kill every Uchiha, huh itachi." *I say as a I stare at the masked man's sharingan*

The masked man lets out a low, dry chuckle that sounds like grinding stones, the sound swallowed quickly by the drumming rain on the limestone shelf. Behind the single hole of the ridged orange mask, the three black tomoe of his Sharingan spin slowly, catching the faint gray ambient light of the storm. "Observant little stray," he murmurs, tilting his head a fraction of an inch. "Though you misunderstand the hierarchy of tonight's work. Your friend here didn't spare me. I helped him finish the chore."

Beside you, Itachi remains completely motionless, his wet black hair plastered against his hollow cheeks, though his hand drops subtly from your chest to rest near the hem of his cloak. "He calls himself Madara," Itachi says quietly, his voice flat and devoid of inflection, though it carries a clear warning not to step out from the overhang. "He was in the compound tonight. And he already agreed that if I brought a partner capable of surviving ANBU black-ops, Akatsuki would have use for another pair of hands."

"I agreed to consider a tool, not a liability whose eyes haven't even woken up yet," 'Madara' replies smoothly, stepping down from the boulder onto the slick stone of the ledge. His boots make no sound at all against the wet rock, and despite the pouring rain, the water seems to slide off his red-cloud cloak without soaking into the fabric. Below the ridge, down in the flooded mud of the border trail, a lantern suddenly bobs into view through the mist—a lone border-post courier in a straw raincoat leading a pack-mule, completely oblivious to the three ghosts perched fifty feet above his head. The mule snorts, its ears pinning back in sudden animal panic at the sheer, suffocating weight of the masked man's chakra bleeding down the cliffside, prompting the courier to curse under his breath and yank the beast's reins faster into the dark.

The masked man doesn't even glance down at the trail; his single crimson eye stays locked on yours, heavy and suffocating, like looking down the barrel of a siege engine. "Blood of the whirlpool and blood of the fan, diluted into something quiet and half-formed," he muses, stopping five paces away where the rain meets the dry shadow of the overhang. "If I let you walk across that border with us, boy, there is no village left to cry for you when you die. Give me one good reason why Pain needs a half-breed with dormant eyes in his ranks, instead of leaving your corpse down on the road for that courier to carry back to Hiruzen."

*I stare at the masked man's eye. trying to figure out who he could be, is he from the village? someone I met before? they way he speaks or carries himself is unique* "so you know who I am? then I don't need to give you a reason."

As you lock your gaze onto that single, shadowed socket, your ANBU training automatically dissects the man behind the swirled orange mask. The legend of Madara Uchiha is a century old—a ghost from the founding era who should be dust or decrepit bone—yet the body beneath the wet red-cloud cloak is in its prime, broad-shouldered and lean, moving with the distinct, grounded balance of someone trained on Konoha's own timber posts. His right arm hangs slightly stiffer than his left, and though his deep baritone is pitched to sound ancient and hollow, the cadence of his Fire Country dialect is unmistakable. You have never passed this man on the streets of the Uchiha compound, nor crossed him in the ANBU locker rooms beneath the Hokage monument, yet he knows the exact lineage of two orphans buried after the Nine-Tails' attack eight years ago.

For a second, the air beneath the limestone overhang grows deathly still. The crimson eye behind the mask narrows a fraction of an inch, the three black tomoe spinning to a dead halt as he registers both your lack of fear and the quiet, probing scrutiny in your stare. Then, without warning, he moves—not with a hand seal or the crack of a Body Flicker, but a silent, impossible step that covers the five paces between you in the blink of an eye, bringing the cold, rain-slicked wood of his mask inches from your face.

Before his gloved hand can rise from the folds of his cloak, the dark canopy two hundred yards back along the ridge explodes in a blinding flash of blue-white electricity. A jagged chorus of chirping lightning—like a thousand frantic birds tearing through the wet pine needles—shatters the roar of the downpour, illuminating the forest in stark, strobing silhouettes. Through the curtain of rain, a lean figure in an ANBU vest with a shock of gravity-defying silver hair bursts across the ravine, his porcelain hound mask pushed up onto his forehead to leave his single uncovered eye—and the glowing red Sharingan in his scarred left socket—completely exposed as he vaults straight toward the scent trail Hana’s hounds marked.

The masked man freezes, his head tilting slightly toward the approaching crackle of the Lightning Blade before his lone eye snaps back to yours, cold and darkly amused. "Kakashi of the Sharingan," 'Madara' murmurs, the air around his own eye beginning to twist into that familiar, hungry spiral as the silver-haired Hound captain closes half the distance to the cliff in a single bound. "Your former commander is faster than Danzo's dogs, boy. Step into the dark with me now, or stay on this rock and explain your scratched headband to the Copy Ninja."
"so in the end, I didn't have to give you a reason" *I say as I get ready to leave with the masked man"

A dry, humorless rasp escapes behind the ridged orange mask as his gloved hand clamps onto your wet shoulder, his fingers cold as grave dirt just as Itachi steps into the inner edge of the vortex beside you. "Arrogant little stray," the masked man murmurs, though the space around his single crimson eye is already tearing open, twisting the rain and the dark stone shelf into a sickening, inward-pulling funnel. "Don't mistake a temporary reprieve for an audition passed."

Fifty yards out, Kakashi hits the slick limestone ridge at a dead sprint, the blue-white snarl of the Lightning Blade carving a smoking trench through the mud and rock as he skids into the clearing. In the harsh, strobing flash of his own jutsu, his uncovered dark eye and the scarred left Sharingan lock directly onto the three of you—taking in Itachi's blood-stained armor, the swirling orange mask, and you standing calmly between them with a gouged forehead protector. For a split second, as the spiraling distortion begins to fold your torso inward like wet paper, Kakashi’s eyes widen in raw, uncomprehending recognition—and at the exact same moment, the masked man’s head tilts a fraction of an inch toward the silver-haired captain, an eerie, silent familiarity hanging between the two mismatched Sharingan before the vortex snaps shut with a deafening *pop* of displaced air.

There is no sensation of falling, only a suffocating pressure that squeezes the breath from your lungs as you are dragged through a pitch-black nowhere of towering, geometric stone pillars, and then spat back out onto solid ground. Your boots hit cracked, damp flagstones, the momentum nearly pitching you forward before you catch your balance. The clean, pine-scented storm of the Land of Fire is gone, replaced by an oppressive, unending sheet of warm, metallic-smelling rain hammering down against rusted iron pipes and towering steel spires that vanish into a low ceiling of smog and bruised purple clouds.

You are standing on a high, corroded balcony jutting out from a massive industrial tower in Amegakure, the Village Hidden in the Rain. A dozen paces away, standing beneath the shelter of a rusted archway where the shadows pool thick and unnatural, two more figures in black red-cloud cloaks are waiting. One is a tall woman with blue hair pinned back by a delicate paper flower, her amber eyes cool and unreadable; beside her stands a lean man with vibrant orange hair, his face lined with black metal piercings that catch the dull neon glow from the streets below—and in his sockets, a pair of concentric, rippled purple eyes look straight through you.

"So this is the prodigy of the Leaf," the pierced man says, his voice echoing like a temple bell across the wet iron grate before those unsettling, ringed eyes shift from Itachi to pin you against the railing. "And a second shadow who wasn't part of our arrangement. Speak quickly, Uchiha—or tell me why the boy beside you shouldn't be drowned in this rain before dawn."
*unbothered, I look over at itachi to see what he answers. even in a situation like this, I feel numb, like maybe dying today would be the right thing to happen*

The warm, rust-tasting rain plasters your hair to your forehead and runs in thin rivulets down the collar of your cloak, yet the chill doesn't reach you. Standing on the corroded iron grate hundreds of feet above Amegakure’s neon-lit canals, the crushing weight of the ringed purple eyes across the balcony feels distant—like pressure behind thick glass. Beside you, Itachi’s profile is carved from pale stone. The blood from the compound has already washed out of his hair and down his neck, leaving only the faint, coppery scent that clings to both of your wet uniforms. He doesn't look back at you, though his left hand shifts half an inch beneath his sleeve, close enough that his knuckles brush the soaked fabric of your forearm—a tiny, silent anchor in the dark.

"His name is Kan," Itachi says, his voice quiet and steady, cutting cleanly through the thrumming din of the rain hitting the iron pipes overhead. "He served under my command in Konoha's Root and ANBU divisions. Tonight, he burned his bridges in front of the Leaf's hunter-nin to leave with me. He doesn't speak unless necessary, he leaves no tracks, and he follows my orders without question."

Behind you, the masked man leans one shoulder against a weeping copper pipe, his arms folded inside his wide sleeves as his single Sharingan gleams from the shadow of his hood. "And he seems entirely ready to let you throw him off this ledge, Pain," 'Madara' adds with a dry, echoing murmur. "Look at his eyes. Half Uchiha, half Uzumaki, and hollow as a gutted fish. A boy who doesn't care if he wakes up tomorrow makes either a very sharp blade... or a very dull shield."

The blue-haired woman—Konan—tilts her head slightly, the white paper flower in her hair remaining bone-dry despite the mist blowing in beneath the archway. Her amber gaze lingers on the stillness of your posture, reading the heavy, hollowed-out exhaustion sitting behind your ribs before she glances sideways at the orange-haired leader. Pain takes a single step forward onto the wet grating, the rain hitting his shoulders as his concentric purple eyes narrow on you with the cold, divine weight of a storm cloud about to break.

"A tool that wishes to break is useless to our peace," Pain intones, raising one hand palm-out toward your chest as the air between you suddenly hums with a strange, gravitational pull that tugs faintly at the iron clasps of your cloak. "If you have nothing left to live for, boy, then your life already belongs to the rain. Tell me yourself—why did you follow Itachi Uchiha into the dark if you only came here to die?"
"I didnt come here to die. I just have nothing left."

For a long beat, only the metallic drum of the downpour fills the balcony, the water sluicing through the rusted iron grating beneath your boots and plummeting into the smog-choked abyss below. The gravitational hum radiating from Pain’s palm doesn't vanish, pulling taut against the wet wool of your cloak and the steel of the tanto strapped across your back, testing whether your knees will buckle or your hand will twitch toward a blade. When you do neither—merely standing there with the warm, rust-scented water running down your face—something shifts in the cold, ringed purple eyes watching you. 

"Nothing left," Pain repeats softly, the resonance of his voice vibrating through the wet iron beneath your soles. Slowly, he lowers his hand, the invisible pressure releasing your chest with a faint, sub-audible sigh of displaced air. "To know that everything you loved can be stripped away in a single night... that is the beginning of true understanding. The great nations hoard their false peace and call it justice, leaving orphans like you to rot in the ashes they create."

Beside him, Konan reaches into the folds of her red-cloud cloak. Before she can draw out whatever she holds, a sudden, metallic *clank* echoes from the maintenance ladder thirty feet down the side of the tower. A hunched Amegakure patrolman in a rubberized rain-poncho and a breather mask pulls himself onto the lower catwalk, a brass wrench in one hand and a flickering oil lamp in the other to check the steam valves. The instant the yellow lamplight catches the red clouds on Pain’s hem above him, the patrolman freezes dead in his tracks. He doesn't shout or reach for a kunai; he immediately drops to both knees on the flooded grate below, pressing his forehead to the wet iron in silent, trembling reverence toward the tower's peak, terrified even to breathe until the "God" and his "Angel" pass.

Neither Pain nor Konan spares the kneeling man a single glance. Instead, Konan extends her pale hand toward you and Itachi, her palm opening to reveal a folded bundle of heavy, dark fabric patterned with crimson clouds, resting beside a single silver ring bearing the etched crimson character for *Scarlet* (*Shu*), and a smaller, unadorned iron band meant for a subordinate's thumb. "The ring is for Uchiha," Konan says, her voice cool and papery against the storm, though her amber eyes remain fixed on you. "And the boy will act as his shadow until he proves he is more than dead weight. Take them, or step off the edge."

jutsuRecords.name: Shinobi taijutsu
jutsuRecords.effect: Close-quarters shinobi combat built for silent takedowns, precise strikes, and quick escapes.
jutsuRecords.visual: Fast, economical movements with almost no sound; Kan closes distance in a low stance and ends exchanges in one or two blows.
jutsuRecords.description: Close-quarters hand-to-hand combat focused on speed, silence, and precision.

jutsuRecords.name: Fire Release
jutsuRecords.effect: Uchiha-affinity fire techniques used to burn, signal, create pressure, or force an enemy back.
jutsuRecords.visual: Chakra ignites into orange-red flames, often leaving heat shimmer and black scorch marks in the air.
jutsuRecords.description: Uchiha-affinity fire techniques used for offense, signals, and pressure.

entities.name: Kan
entities.personality: Quiet, timid, stoic, smart, hides his feelings.
entities.speechStyle: Short, restrained, rarely volunteers more than necessary.
entities.notes: Original character. Uchiha-Uzumaki lineage, usually goes only by Kan. Itachi has been his only friend outside Team 3 since toddlerhood.
entities.appearance: Lean teenage shinobi with black hair, dark watchful eyes, wearing a plain black high-collared shinobi outfit with bandage-wrapped forearms. No ANBU gear.

entities.name: Itachi Uchiha
entities.personality: Calm, perceptive, self-sacrificing, gentle beneath a controlled surface.
entities.speechStyle: Quiet, precise, polite, often speaking in gentle observations.
entities.notes: Kan’s closest friend, like an older brother. Joined ANBU one year before Kan. Known Kan since he was a toddler.
entities.mood: Burdened, controlled, grieving beneath the calm
entities.appearance: Slim young man with long black hair tied back, sharp dark eyes, tear troughs, and a black cloak patterned with red clouds.

entities.name: Hana Inuzuka
entities.personality: Loud, loyal, instinctive, protective, quick to act.
entities.speechStyle: Direct, blunt, teasing, with little patience for hesitation.
entities.notes: Kan’s teammate. He has a secret crush on her.
entities.appearance: Athletic girl with tousled brown hair, fang-like markings on her cheeks, and a practical Inuzuka jacket.

entities.name: Izumi Uchiha
entities.speechStyle: Soft and careful, with a warm teasing streak.
entities.appearance: Young Uchiha girl with soft dark hair, gentle eyes, and the quiet posture of someone who always waited for others.

entities.name: Suzume
entities.personality: Patient, sharp, protective, demanding in the field.
entities.appearance: Seasoned jonin woman with practical field clothes, tied-back hair, and the calm stance of a teacher who has buried students.

entities.name: Forest outside Konoha
entities.notes: Rain-soaked meeting place after the Uchiha massacre.

entities.name: Akatsuki
entities.notes: Itachi wants Kan to join as an inside spy.

entities.name: Madara (Masked Man)
entities.role: Shadow leader of Akatsuki / Accomplice in the Uchiha Massacre
entities.speechStyle: Deep, resonant baritone; speaks with ancient authority and mocking detachment
entities.appearance: Tall figure in a black Akatsuki cloak with red clouds, wearing a ridged orange mask with a single eye-hole revealing a spinning Sharingan.

entities.name: Pain
entities.speechStyle: Deep, resonant, authoritative; speaks in absolutes about pain, peace, and utility
entities.appearance: A lean man with spiked orange hair, numerous black chakra rods piercing his nose, ears, and lip, wearing the black Akatsuki cloak with red clouds, possessing the purple concentric rings of the Rinnegan.

entities.name: Konan
entities.personality: Calm, observant, fiercely loyal to Pain, reserved
entities.appearance: A tall woman with blue hair pinned in a bun with an intricate white origami flower, amber eyes, a single labret piercing beneath her lip, wearing the red-cloud Akatsuki cloak.

events.summary: Kan waits alone in the rain-soaked forest outside Konoha after the Uchiha massacre. He does not yet know Shisui is dead. Itachi is about to arrive and ask him to join Akatsuki.

bonds.note: Kan agreed to leave Konoha with Itachi to infiltrate Akatsuki together.
Kan hides his feelings and has never told her.

facts.text: Kan’s parents, Erisa and Banri, died in the Nine-Tails attack.
Kan was five years old when the Nine-Tails attacked.
Kan joined ANBU at age 12, one year after Itachi.
Kan has a crush on Hana Inuzuka and has never told her.
Killed during the Uchiha clan massacre, as confirmed by Itachi stating only Sasuke survived.
Itachi killed Izumi first during the massacre using his Mangekyo Sharingan genjutsu so she lived out a peaceful lifetime before dying painlessly. (known by: Itachi, Kan)
Hana and her ninken are part of the four-man hunter cell pursuing Itachi outside Konoha on the night of the massacre.
Decided to abandon Konoha with Itachi because Hana's ninken would detect their scents meeting in the forest, making a return to the village impossible under Danzo's scrutiny.
Intercepted Itachi and Kan at the limestone ridge outside Konoha on the night of the Uchiha massacre, questioning Kan's presence and threatening to kill him as a loose end.
Revealed to Kan that he claims to be Madara Uchiha and participated in the Uchiha clan massacre alongside Itachi.
Knows of Kan's mixed Uzumaki and Uchiha heritage ('blood of the whirlpool and blood of the fan').
Noticed that the masked man calling himself Madara has the physique and speech cadence of a modern Konoha-trained shinobi rather than an ancient elder, and knows Kan's secret Uzumaki-Uchiha lineage.
Pursued Itachi and Kan to the border ridge on the night of the Uchiha massacre using his Lightning Blade.
Witnessed Kan defecting alongside Itachi Uchiha and the masked man ('Madara') on the limestone ridge outside Konoha.
Was transported via the masked man's space-time jutsu from the Land of Fire border directly to Amegakure to meet Pain and Konan.

threads.title: What really happened to Shisui?
threads.description: Kan does not yet know Shisui is dead and wants to understand what happened.

threads.title: Find a reason to keep going after the massacre
threads.description: Kan has left the village and is hiding in the woods, waiting for Itachi.

loreEntries.text: Kan is of mixed Uchiha-Uzumaki heritage. His Uchiha mother and Uzumaki father died in the Nine-Tails attack. He rarely mentions his clan names. He has not yet awakened the Sharingan.
The Nine-Tails attack killed Kan’s parents when he was five. It left him quiet, stoic, and reluctant to rely on others.
ANBU are Konoha’s masked special forces. Kan joined at twelve, one year after Itachi. He is no longer part of ANBU — he left the village and carries no ANBU equipment.

summaries.text: On a rain-soaked limestone ridge, Kan confronts Itachi about Izumi's death. Itachi admits he killed her peacefully, his Sharingan briefly bleeding into a strange new pattern. Before Kan can press further, Hana Inuzuka and an ANBU cell close in, the Haimaru triplets tracking their scent. Itachi offers Kan a kunai and a final choice: return to Konoha or flee with him. Kan drops his ANBU mask into the mud and scratches his forehead protector, severing his ties to the Leaf as Hana watches in disbelief.

On the night of the Uchiha massacre, Kan makes his choice. At Itachi's urging—"Scratch your headband, or leave the mask in the mud"—Kan drops his ANBU mask into the mud and gouges his forehead protector, severing his ties in full view of Hana Inuzuka and her boar-masked ANBU captain. Hana's stunned "Kan?" is cut off by the captain's Fire Style attack; Itachi's Body Flicker drags Kan into the canopy, embers scalding his face. The Haimaru triplets' baying fades.

Three miles out on a limestone ridge, a masked man with a single Sharingan spirals out of the rain, calling himself Madara.

player.name: Kan
secretNotes: Has a secret crush on Hana Inuzuka.

state.worldDescription: The Hidden Leaf is scarred by the Nine-Tails attack and freshly wounded by the Uchiha massacre. The village is tense, watchful, and rebuilding in silence.
state.location: Amegakure (Village Hidden in the Rain) - High industrial balcony
state.canonPoint: Arriving in Amegakure before Pain and Konan after escaping Kakashi Hatake
